---
title: "Understanding Interfaces in C#"
---

Let me elaborate on interfaces with clear examples and diagrams.


## What is an Interface?

An interface is like a **contract** or **blueprint** that defines *what* a class must do, but not *how* it does it.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      INTERFACE                              │
│                                                             │
│   "I promise to have these abilities"                       │
│                                                             │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │  • Method signatures (no implementation)            │   │
│   │  • Property signatures                              │   │
│   │  • Event signatures                                 │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            │ implements
                            ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        CLASS                                │
│                                                             │
│   "I fulfill the promise with actual code"                  │
│                                                             │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │  • Actual method implementations                    │   │
│   │  • Property implementations with backing fields     │   │
│   │  • Event implementations                            │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```


## Basic Interface Syntax

```csharp
// Define an interface (by convention, starts with "I")
public interface IExaminable
{
    // Property signature (no backing field allowed)
    string ExamType { get; }
    
    // Method signature (no body in traditional interfaces)
    void PerformExam();
    
    // Another method
    string GetReport();
}

// A class that implements the interface
public class CTScan : IExaminable
{
    // MUST implement all interface members
    public string ExamType => "CT Scan";
    
    public void PerformExam()
    {
        Console.WriteLine("Performing CT scan...");
    }
    
    public string GetReport()
    {
        return "CT findings: Normal study";
    }
}
```


## "Can Do" vs "Has A" Relationships

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        RELATIONSHIP TYPES                          │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                    │
│  "CAN DO" (Capability)              "HAS A" (Possession)           │
│  ─────────────────────              ─────────────────────          │
│                                                                    │
│  IComparable                        IEnumerable                    │
│    └─> "I CAN compare myself"         └─> "I HAVE items to list"  │
│                                                                    │
│  IDisposable                        ICollection                    │
│    └─> "I CAN clean up resources"     └─> "I HAVE a collection"   │
│                                                                    │
│  ICloneable                                                        │
│    └─> "I CAN clone myself"                                        │
│                                                                    │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```


## Practical Example: Medical Imaging Context

Let me create an example relevant to your radiology background:

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;

// ============================================================
// INTERFACE DEFINITIONS
// ============================================================

// "Can Do" interface - ability to be reported
public interface IReportable
{
    string GenerateReport();
    DateTime ReportDate { get; }
}

// "Can Do" interface - ability to be compared (for sorting)
public interface IComparable<T>
{
    int CompareTo(T other);
}

// "Has A" interface - has measurements
public interface IMeasurable
{
    List<Measurement> Measurements { get; }
    void AddMeasurement(Measurement m);
}

// ============================================================
// SUPPORTING CLASSES
// ============================================================

public class Measurement
{
    public string Name { get; set; }
    public double Value { get; set; }
    public string Unit { get; set; }
    
    public override string ToString() => $"{Name}: {Value} {Unit}";
}

// ============================================================
// CLASS IMPLEMENTING MULTIPLE INTERFACES
// ============================================================

public class RadiologyStudy : IReportable, IMeasurable, IComparable<RadiologyStudy>
{
    public string PatientId { get; set; }
    public string Modality { get; set; }  // CT, MRI, X-Ray, etc.
    public DateTime StudyDate { get; set; }
    public DateTime ReportDate { get; private set; }
    
    // IMeasurable implementation
    public List<Measurement> Measurements { get; } = new List<Measurement>();
    
    public void AddMeasurement(Measurement m)
    {
        Measurements.Add(m);
    }
    
    // IReportable implementation
    public string GenerateReport()
    {
        ReportDate = DateTime.Now;
        var report = $"""
            === RADIOLOGY REPORT ===
            Patient: {PatientId}
            Modality: {Modality}
            Study Date: {StudyDate:yyyy-MM-dd}
            
            Measurements:
            {string.Join("\n", Measurements)}
            
            Report Generated: {ReportDate:yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm}
            """;
        return report;
    }
    
    // IComparable implementation (sort by study date)
    public int CompareTo(RadiologyStudy other)
    {
        if (other == null) return 1;
        return StudyDate.CompareTo(other.StudyDate);
    }
}
```


## Using the Interfaces

```csharp
class Program
{
    static void Main()
    {
        // Create a study
        var ctStudy = new RadiologyStudy
        {
            PatientId = "HN-12345",
            Modality = "CT",
            StudyDate = DateTime.Now
        };
        
        // Use IMeasurable capability
        ctStudy.AddMeasurement(new Measurement 
        { 
            Name = "Liver lesion", 
            Value = 2.5, 
            Unit = "cm" 
        });
        ctStudy.AddMeasurement(new Measurement 
        { 
            Name = "Aorta diameter", 
            Value = 28, 
            Unit = "mm" 
        });
        
        // Use IReportable capability
        Console.WriteLine(ctStudy.GenerateReport());
        
        // ================================================
        // THE POWER OF INTERFACES: Polymorphism
        // ================================================
        
        // You can treat any IReportable the same way!
        PrintReport(ctStudy);
    }
    
    // This method works with ANY class that implements IReportable
    static void PrintReport(IReportable reportable)
    {
        Console.WriteLine("Generating report...");
        Console.WriteLine(reportable.GenerateReport());
    }
}
```


## Key Restrictions Explained

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    INTERFACE RESTRICTIONS                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                 │
│  ❌ NO Constructors                                             │
│     interface IExample { IExample(); }  // NOT ALLOWED          │
│                                                                 │
│  ❌ NO Fields                                                   │
│     interface IExample { private int x; }  // NOT ALLOWED       │
│                                                                 │
│  ❌ NO Static Members (traditionally)                           │
│     interface IExample { static void Do(); }  // NOT ALLOWED*   │
│                                                                 │
│  ✅ Members are implicitly PUBLIC                               │
│     interface IExample { void Do(); }  // Always public         │
│                                                                 │
│  * Note: C# 8+ allows static abstract members in interfaces     │
│    for advanced scenarios (generic math, etc.)                  │
│                                                                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```


## Common .NET Interfaces You'll Use

| Interface | Purpose | Key Method |
|-----------|---------|------------|
| `IComparable<T>` | Enable sorting | `CompareTo(T other)` |
| `IEquatable<T>` | Custom equality | `Equals(T other)` |
| `IEnumerable<T>` | Enable `foreach` | `GetEnumerator()` |
| `IDisposable` | Resource cleanup | `Dispose()` |
| `ICloneable` | Object copying | `Clone()` |


## Default Interface Methods (C# 8+)

Since you're on .NET 9, you can use **default implementations**:

```csharp
public interface IReportable
{
    string GenerateReport();
    DateTime ReportDate { get; }
    
    // Default implementation - classes don't HAVE to override this
    void PrintReport()
    {
        Console.WriteLine("=== REPORT ===");
        Console.WriteLine(GenerateReport());
    }
}
```

This allows interfaces to evolve without breaking existing implementations.


## Why Use Interfaces?

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    BENEFITS OF INTERFACES                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                 │
│  1. MULTIPLE "INHERITANCE"                                      │
│     └─> A class can implement many interfaces                   │
│         (but can only inherit from ONE base class)              │
│                                                                 │
│  2. LOOSE COUPLING                                              │
│     └─> Code depends on contracts, not implementations          │
│     └─> Easy to swap implementations (great for testing!)       │
│                                                                 │
│  3. POLYMORPHISM                                                │
│     └─> Treat different classes uniformly                       │
│     └─> Process collections of different types                  │
│                                                                 │
│  4. API DESIGN                                                  │
│     └─> Define what consumers can do without exposing HOW       │
│                                                                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
